title: Metabo-Diet posttest
instructions: Complete after all five lessons and the notebook. The delivery platform should hide answers and rationales until submission.

scoring.mastery_note: Learners below threshold should review feedback by objective and retry with a parallel item set before any certificate is issued.

items.prompt: The ST001521 factors response contains 160 rows. Which interpretation is supported by the module audit?

options.B: There are 150 participant-timepoint rows and 10 pooled QPP quality-control rows in the current record.
options.C: There are 40 participants measured four times.
options.D: The 10 QPP rows should be treated as a fourth diet group.

items.rationale: The study describes 30 participants at five biological times, and the factor table includes 10 QPP pooled QC candidates. QC rows do not increase participant count.

items.prompt: How should the ST001521 plasma and ST003348 serum specimens be handled?

options.A: Rename both blood and pool their peak areas.
options.B: Keep exact matrix labels, optionally use a broader blood-derived-fluid category for discovery, and prohibit matrix-equivalent quantitative pooling.
options.D: Convert serum to plasma using z-scores.

items.rationale: A broad category can support discovery, but serum and plasma remain distinct pre-analytical matrices and scaling is not a conversion.

items.prompt: Why should ST001521 Day 9 not be mapped to ST003348 REC3 as a generic post timepoint?

options.B: Day 9 belongs to a feeding and antibiotic/PEG protocol, while REC3 is 3 hours after an endurance exercise bout.

items.rationale: The labels have different anchor events, offsets, and physiological meanings. Collapsing them to post would erase the central design context.

items.prompt: Which statement best describes a direct cross-study diet-versus-exercise quantitative contrast?

options.A: It isolates phenotype because both studies use LC-MS.
options.B: It is confounded by study, population, matrix, laboratory, platform implementation, time, and protocol, so the module does not use it for causal inference.
options.C: It becomes causal after RefMet mapping.
options.D: It is valid whenever sample sizes exceed 20.

items.rationale: Phenotype anchor is inseparable from many study-specific differences. Neither shared technology labels nor sample size solves that confounding.

items.prompt: ST003348 contains isotope/internal-standard labels that map to ordinary RefMet names. What should the biological overlap workflow do?

options.A: Count them as endogenous overlaps because RefMet is nonblank.
options.B: Preserve the source labels, classify their nonbiological analytical role, and exclude them from biological overlap with a reason.
options.D: Use them to calibrate ST001521 automatically.

items.rationale: The crosswalk must preserve isotope/standard identity and prevent a standardized ordinary name from creating a false endogenous overlap.

items.prompt: Two source features in one analysis map to the same RefMet name. What is the reproducible approach?

options.A: Average their intensities immediately and discard source IDs.
options.B: Keep feature-level rows and provenance, flag the many-to-one mapping, and define a separate collapse rule for any set-level summary.
options.C: Choose the feature with the larger mean.
options.D: Count the RefMet name twice in the overlap set.

items.rationale: Feature identity and mapping cardinality must remain auditable. A set-level unique key is different from a quantitative feature-collapse decision.

items.prompt: Which overlap report matches the audited module build?

options.B: 153 shared nonblank exact RefMet strings before exclusions; 145 in the conservative biological set after excluding eight ST003348 isotope/internal-standard rows, with all rules versioned
options.D: The overlap is undefined because no names can ever be compared

items.rationale: The two counts answer different audit stages. The conservative set removes eight nonbiological mappings, but neither count implies shared concentration or response.

items.prompt: Which PCA plan follows the module guardrails?

options.A: Fit separate, documented within-study PCAs; keep repeated measures and sample roles visible; do not stack the uncalibrated raw matrices.
options.B: Pool both studies and label the first component diet versus exercise.
options.C: Include pooled QPP samples as participants.
options.D: Hide preprocessing because PCA is objective.

items.rationale: Separate within-study PCA limits scale mixing and supports design-aware exploration. A combined study contrast cannot uniquely attribute separation.

items.prompt: The live REST request fails and the notebook uses a cached response. What must the analysis report?

options.A: Nothing; cache use is invisible to learners.
options.B: The failed endpoint/status, cached retrieval time, integrity check, and a visible cached-source flag.

items.rationale: A cache preserves continuity but must not masquerade as current live retrieval. Provenance and integrity evidence are required.

items.prompt: How should MoTrPAC access be described when transferring this workflow?

options.C: Dataset- and release-dependent, with public and restricted paths that require a current first-party check
options.D: Available only through the Metabolomics Workbench REST API

items.rationale: Current MoTrPAC documentation distinguishes public access from restricted or embargoed pathways. The exact desired release and action control the plan.

items.prompt: What is the appropriate default plan for participant-level NPH data in All of Us?

options.A: Copy data to the module's public cache.
options.B: Run approved code in the Researcher Workbench, keep governed data there, and export only policy-permitted outputs after checking current requirements.

items.rationale: NPH participant-level work uses the governed Researcher Workbench. Code and permitted references can move in; governed data stay and outputs follow current policy.

items.prompt: A crosswalk join unexpectedly doubles the number of measurement rows. What should happen next?

options.A: Proceed because more rows improve power.
options.C: Stop, inspect key uniqueness and join cardinality, and revise the documented join rule before analysis.
options.D: Average all values across both studies.

items.rationale: Unexpected row multiplication usually signals a one-to-many or many-to-many key problem. It must be diagnosed rather than hidden.
